episodes.title: Programs become processes
episodes.description: Follow a program from disk into memory, see what fork and exec change, and trace parent and child processes.
topics: From a program file to a process
Read process trees and fork traces

chapters.title: From a program file to a process
Read process trees and fork traces

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Welcome to CSQuest Audio. I'm Maya, here with Leo. This section is called Programs become processes.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: From booting the computer to creating a running program.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: follow a program from disk into memory, see what fork and exec change, and trace parent and child processes.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with operating systems and computer startup and work our way to exec replaces a process image.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's start with operating systems and computer startup. What do we need to know?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An operating system is the trusted software layer that starts the machine, manages hardware and gives applications safe, useful services.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Hardware means the physical processor, memory and devices.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: When you open a photo, the app asks the OS to read file blocks, allocate memory and schedule its instructions on the CPU.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A process is not a program file.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to from a program file to a process. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A program file is passive instructions stored on disk; a process is one active execution with its own state and resources.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Program means a stored set of instructions; it does not run by itself.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: From program file to process · Discover: A loader starts a program with three initialized data values, what must exist for this running instance to resume after it is paused?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Saved process state such as registers and a program counter. A program file is passive instructions stored on disk; a process is one active execution with its own state and resources.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: fork creates a child process from a running parent; both continue after the call with separate return values.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Parent means the process that calls fork.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: After one successful fork, a print statement reached by both processes can run twice, though their order is not fixed.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Fork creates a process; exec replaces the running program image.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A fork trace is a branching execution tree: only processes that reach a fork create another child.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Execution path means the instructions one process reaches in order.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Tracing fork trees · Discover: A program starts with one process; each of its two branches reaches one more fork, how many processes exist after both second forks succeed?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Four. A fork trace is a branching execution tree: only processes that reach a fork create another child.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain exec replaces a process image to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: exec loads a new program into the current process, replacing its code and data while the process keeps its identity.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Process image means the code, data and stack currently loaded for a process.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A command shell can keep its process identity while replacing its image with the requested command.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave programs become processes, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An operating system is the trusted software layer that starts the machine, manages hardware and gives applications safe, useful services.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: exec loads a new program into the current process, replacing its code and data while the process keeps its identity.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We've covered a lot in programs become processes. You don't have to remember every detail at once; start by trying one of the examples yourself.

episodes.subject: os
episodes.title: Threads and CPU scheduling
episodes.description: Compare processes and threads, read the ready queue, and simulate CPU scheduling by hand.
topics: Scheduling mixed CPU and I/O bursts

chapters.title: Scheduling mixed CPU and I/O bursts

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hi, I'm Maya. Leo's with me, and today's section is called Threads and CPU scheduling.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Share a processor fairly and keep work moving.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: compare processes and threads, read the ready queue, and simulate CPU scheduling by hand.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with user mode and kernel mode and work our way to priority scheduling and starvation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to user mode and kernel mode. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Applications run with limited privileges and request protected operations through system calls handled by the kernel.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: User mode means a restricted CPU mode for application instructions.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: read asks the kernel to copy bytes from an open file into a process buffer after checking access and arguments.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A process is not a program file.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: user and kernel threads.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Threads are execution paths within a process; they share process resources but each needs its own instruction position and stack.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Thread means a schedulable path of execution with its own registers and stack.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: User-level and kernel-level threads · Discover: Two threads belong to one process and update different local variables, which resource is private to each thread during execution?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Its register state and stack. Threads are execution paths within a process; they share process resources but each needs its own instruction position and stack.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A thread mapping determines how user threads correspond to kernel-scheduled threads; a context switch saves one execution and restores another.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Many-to-one means many user threads map to one kernel thread.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: With many-to-one mapping, one blocking system call can block the only kernel thread and stall every user thread in that process.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A process moves among states as it waits for CPU time, requests I/O and finishes; different schedulers make decisions at different timescales.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Ready means able to run, waiting for a CPU.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Process states and schedulers · Discover: A running process requests disk I/O and its data is not ready yet, what state should it enter while waiting?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Blocked. A process moves among states as it waits for CPU time, requests I/O and finishes; different schedulers make decisions at different timescales.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Blocked is not ready.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack scheduling goals and FCFS next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A CPU scheduler chooses a ready process; scheduling metrics describe different costs experienced by each job.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Arrival time means when a process enters the ready system.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: If a job arrives at time 2 and finishes at time 9, its turnaround is 7 time units.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A timeline must respect arrivals, remaining burst time and the scheduling rule.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: SJF chooses the ready job with the shortest next CPU burst; preemptive SRTF can replace it when a shorter remaining job arrives.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: CPU burst means a stretch of computation before waiting or yielding.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Shortest-job-first scheduling · Discover: Two jobs arrive together with CPU bursts 6 and 2, which job runs first under non-preemptive SJF?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The 2-unit burst. SJF chooses the ready job with the shortest next CPU burst; preemptive SRTF can replace it when a shorter remaining job arrives.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Round-robin scheduling gives each ready process up to one time quantum, then moves unfinished work to the queue tail.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Time quantum means the maximum CPU time in one round-robin turn.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: With a quantum of 3, a process needing 8 CPU units runs for 3, returns to the tail, and needs 5 more.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's start with scheduling mixed CPU and I/O bursts. What do we need to know?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Processes alternate between CPU bursts and I/O waits; completion of I/O moves a blocked process back to the ready queue.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: CPU burst means work executed on a processor.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: CPU and I/O bursts in scheduling · Discover: Process A blocks for I/O while process B is ready, what should the scheduler do with the idle CPU?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Run B while A waits for its I/O event. Processes alternate between CPU bursts and I/O waits; completion of I/O moves a blocked process back to the ready queue.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Priority scheduling favors higher-priority ready jobs; aging gradually raises long-waiting jobs to prevent starvation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Priority means a rank used to choose among ready processes.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: If smaller numbers mean higher priority, a job at priority 5 may wait behind a stream of new priority-1 jobs unless aging helps it.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave threads and CPU scheduling, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Applications run with limited privileges and request protected operations through system calls handled by the kernel.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Priority scheduling favors higher-priority ready jobs; aging gradually raises long-waiting jobs to prevent starvation.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Try explaining priority scheduling and starvation in your own words. If you get stuck, that chapter is a good place to listen again.

episodes.subject: os
episodes.title: Communication and synchronization
episodes.description: Make shared data safe with critical sections, atomic operations, locks and semaphores.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Welcome back. Maya here, with Leo. We've reached the section called Communication and synchronization.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Coordinate concurrent work without races or deadlock.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: make shared data safe with critical sections, atomic operations, locks and semaphores.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with interprocess communication and work our way to readers, writers and dining philosophers.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: interprocess communication.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Processes communicate by sharing a memory region or exchanging messages through operating-system mechanisms.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Shared memory means a region mapped so multiple processes can read or write it.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A producer can place records in shared memory, but both processes still need a rule for when a record is complete.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on concurrency and race conditions.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Concurrent instructions can interleave; a race occurs when the result depends on the timing of accesses to shared data.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Interleaving means an order that mixes steps from concurrent executions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Concurrency and race conditions · Discover: Two workers each increment the same counter using separate read and write steps, what final value can occur if both read zero before either write?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: 1. Concurrent instructions can interleave; a race occurs when the result depends on the timing of accesses to shared data.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A read-modify-write sequence is not automatically atomic.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A critical section protects shared data; a correct protocol needs mutual exclusion, progress and bounded waiting.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Mutual exclusion means at most one process is in the critical section at a time.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A bank balance update should not let two transfers overwrite each other’s changes.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Mutual exclusion alone does not guarantee fairness.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A synchronization protocol must both keep conflicting work out of the critical section and let waiting work make progress.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Safety means nothing bad happens, such as two owners entering together.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Testing critical-section protocols · Discover: A lock allows one owner in but permanently ignores every later request, which property does that behavior violate?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Progress. A synchronization protocol must both keep conflicting work out of the critical section and let waiting work make progress.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Now for peterson’s solution. What's the key distinction?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Peterson’s algorithm uses one intent flag per process and a turn variable to coordinate two processes under its memory-order assumptions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Intent flag means a shared Boolean stating that a process wants to enter.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: If both processes raise their flags, turn breaks the tie so one waits while the other enters.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Atomic read-modify-write instructions let software update a lock without another processor slipping between the read and write.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Test-and-set means atomically reads a lock value and sets it.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Atomic hardware operations · Discover: Two CPU cores try to acquire the same lock simultaneously, what feature makes only one atomic test-and-set observe the old unlocked value?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The instruction executes indivisibly across the competing cores. Atomic read-modify-write instructions let software update a lock without another processor slipping between the read and write.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A semaphore is an integer-like synchronization object whose wait and signal operations coordinate permits or events.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: wait means take a permit or block until one becomes available.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A semaphore initialized to 3 can allow up to three workers to use a pool of three identical resources.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to producer-consumer buffers. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A bounded buffer uses empty-slot, full-slot and mutual-exclusion semaphores to coordinate producers and consumers safely.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: empty means the number of unused buffer slots.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Bounded producer-consumer buffer · Discover: A four-slot buffer contains three items before a producer inserts one, how many empty slots remain afterward?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: 0. A bounded buffer uses empty-slot, full-slot and mutual-exclusion semaphores to coordinate producers and consumers safely.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Readers-writers and dining philosophers model competing access to shared resources and reveal starvation and deadlock risks.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Reader means a process that observes shared data without changing it.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: If every philosopher picks up one fork and waits for the other, the resource graph can form a cycle.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Fork creates a process; exec replaces the running program image.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave communication and synchronization, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Processes communicate by sharing a memory region or exchanging messages through operating-system mechanisms.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Readers-writers and dining philosophers model competing access to shared resources and reveal starvation and deadlock risks.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: When you try a problem on readers, writers and dining philosophers, talk through why each step works. That's a useful check on what has clicked.

episodes.subject: os
episodes.title: Memory and virtual addresses
episodes.description: Trace segmentation and paging, calculate address translation costs, and model page replacement.
topics: TLB, dirty pages and page-fault costs

chapters.title: TLB, dirty pages and page-fault costs

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I'm Maya, and this is CSQuest Audio. Today, Leo and I are taking on Memory and virtual addresses.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Translate addresses, keep pages close and respond to misses.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: trace segmentation and paging, calculate address translation costs, and model page replacement.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with base and bounds, then segmentation and work our way to TLB, dirty pages and page-fault costs.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on base and bounds, then segmentation.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A base and bound pair confines addresses to one process region; segmentation gives code, data and stack separate variable-sized regions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Base means the physical start address of a region.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: For base 4000 and length 600, logical offset 120 maps to 4120, while offset 700 is outside the bound.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain segmentation examples and fragmentation to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Variable-sized segments can leave free memory split into gaps; total free space may be large enough while no single gap is large enough.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: External fragmentation means free memory exists in separated holes that cannot fit one requested block.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Segmentation and external fragmentation · Discover: Memory has free holes of 4 and 5 units and a request needs 7 contiguous units, can the request fit without compaction?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: No. Variable-sized segments can leave free memory split into gaps; total free space may be large enough while no single gap is large enough.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Paging divides virtual memory into fixed-size pages and physical memory into equal-size frames; a page table maps one to the other.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Page means a fixed-size block of a process virtual address space.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: With 256-byte pages, address 600 is page 2 with offset 88 because 600 = 2×256 + 88.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A flat page table stores one entry for each virtual page, so address width and page size determine its entry count.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Virtual address means an address generated by a process.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Single-level page-table calculations · Discover: A 16-bit virtual address uses 256-byte pages, how many page-number bits remain?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: 8 bits. A flat page table stores one entry for each virtual page, so address width and page size determine its entry count.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We also need to talk about multilevel page tables.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A multilevel page table splits virtual page-number bits into indexes so unused branches need not allocate lower-level tables.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Page-directory index means the first group of page-number bits used to choose a table.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A two-level walk first selects a page-directory entry, then a page-table entry, then uses the offset in the frame.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A multilevel translation follows each page-table index in order and appends the original offset to the final frame number.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Page walk means the sequence of memory reads needed to follow page tables.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Walking multilevel translations · Discover: A two-level translation performs two table reads followed by one data read, how many memory reads occur without a translation cache?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: 3. A multilevel translation follows each page-table index in order and appends the original offset to the final frame number.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Page tables trade memory space against lookup work; a translation lookaside buffer caches recent mappings to avoid repeated walks.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Flat page table means one entry for every virtual page.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A TLB hit can find a frame quickly; a miss needs a page-table walk before the requested data access.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A TLB miss is not necessarily a page fault.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Page offsets are preserved during translation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: reviewing memory allocation schemes.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Contiguous regions, segmentation and paging make different tradeoffs in protection, flexibility and fragmentation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Contiguous allocation means give a process one adjacent physical region.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Review memory allocation schemes · Discover: A process needs 10 bytes and receives a fixed 8-byte page size, how many bytes are unused in its final allocated page?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: 6 bytes. Contiguous regions, segmentation and paging make different tradeoffs in protection, flexibility and fragmentation.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Segmented paging first selects a segment’s page table, then maps a page within that segment to a frame.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Segment number means the logical region being addressed.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A logical address can select segment 2, page 3, offset 12; the segment table locates the page table before frame translation.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Demand paging loads a page when it is first accessed; if memory is full, a replacement policy chooses a resident page to evict.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Page fault means a trap caused by accessing a page that is not currently mapped in memory.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Demand paging and page replacement · Discover: Frames hold pages 1 and 2; a reference requests absent page 3, what event is raised before page 3 can be read?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A page fault. Demand paging loads a page when it is first accessed; if memory is full, a replacement policy chooses a resident page to evict.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack TLBs and virtual-memory performance next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A translation lookaside buffer caches address translations; effective access time depends on hit rate and the costs of hits and misses.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: TLB hit means the translation is found in the translation cache.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: If a hit costs 10 ns and a miss path costs 110 ns, a 90% hit rate gives 20 ns average: 0.9×10 + 0.1×110.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A dirty victim has been modified; eviction must write it back before the requested page can be read into its frame.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Dirty bit means a flag showing that a memory page changed since it was loaded.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Dirty pages and page-fault cost · Discover: A dirty victim takes 8 ms to write and the new page takes 12 ms to read, what storage time is required before execution resumes?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: 20 ms. A dirty victim has been modified; eviction must write it back before the requested page can be read into its frame.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave memory and virtual addresses, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A base and bound pair confines addresses to one process region; segmentation gives code, data and stack separate variable-sized regions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A dirty victim has been modified; eviction must write it back before the requested page can be read into its frame.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Take a small example of base and bounds, then segmentation and work it out before looking at the explanation. Then compare your reasoning.

chapters.title: Deadlock prevention, avoidance and Banker’s algorithm

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Maya and Leo here. Our section today is Deadlocks and file systems.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Allocate resources safely and find data on storage.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: recognize deadlock, test safe allocations, and follow files from a name to disk blocks.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with deadlock conditions and resource graphs and work our way to file-system implementation practice.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain deadlock conditions and resource graphs to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Deadlock is a set of processes waiting forever; four conditions must all hold for deadlock to be possible.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Mutual exclusion means at least one resource can be held by only one process at a time.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: P1 holds printer and waits for scanner while P2 holds scanner and waits for printer; neither can proceed.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A cycle implies deadlock in a single-instance resource graph, but not generally with multiple instances.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack deadlock prevention, avoidance and Banker’s algorithm next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Banker’s algorithm grants a resource request only when the remaining needs can still be satisfied in some safe completion order.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Available means currently free instances of each resource type.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Banker’s algorithm and safe states · Discover: A process needs at most 2 more units and 3 are currently available, can its remaining need be satisfied now?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Yes. Banker’s algorithm grants a resource request only when the remaining needs can still be satisfied in some safe completion order.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A file system maps human-readable names to metadata and disk blocks using an allocation strategy.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Directory means a mapping from names to file metadata or entries.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An indexed file can reach block 90 through its index even when its data blocks are not adjacent.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Storage performance depends on how a file maps to blocks and how the disk device orders requests.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Seek means movement of a disk head to a track or cylinder.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: File-system and disk scheduling practice · Discover: A disk head is at cylinder 40 and the next request is cylinder 46, how many cylinders of movement are required?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: 6. Storage performance depends on how a file maps to blocks and how the disk device orders requests.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave deadlocks and file systems, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Deadlock is a set of processes waiting forever; four conditions must all hold for deadlock to be possible.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Storage performance depends on how a file maps to blocks and how the disk device orders requests.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: You can pause here and try the Deadlocks and file systems activities. Pick one idea and see whether you can explain it without the notes.
